extracted.intended_audience: readers and contributors of Nature (scientists, authors, and publishers of scientific books; correspondents submitting letters)
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and evaluative criteria used by Nature reviewers and the Editor when assessing books (biographies, textbooks, multi-author volumes, translations, practical manuals, ethnographies) and letters to the Editor, covering accuracy, usefulness, presentation, production quality, and submission rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editor responsibility and submission policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The Editor does not hold himself responsible for opinions expressed by his correspondents. Neither can he undertake to return, or to correspond with the writers of, rejected manuscripts intended for this or any other part of Nature. No notice is taken of anonymous communications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions should be signed (not anonymous). Authors should not expect returned manuscripts or personalized correspondence about rejected pieces; editorial disclaimer of responsibility for views expressed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequate treatment of subject-matter
rubrics_metrics.description: The history of the educational institutions of the town receives adequate treatment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A work should give sufficient and appropriate coverage of its primary subject so readers obtain a satisfactory account rather than a cursory summary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suitability as a visitor's guide / pleasantness for intended visitors
rubrics_metrics.description: Intending visitors would find in it a pleasanter account of their place of meeting than the pages of an ordinary guide-book can afford.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For works aimed at visitors, prefer pleasant, readable accounts with local color and usefulness beyond a standard guidebook.

rubrics_metrics.name: Illustrations and index presence/quality
rubrics_metrics.description: The book is admirably illustrated, and is provided with an Index.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High-quality, relevant illustrations and a functioning index increase a book's utility; illustrations should be placed and referenced appropriately (see production-quality criteria).

rubrics_metrics.name: Readability and stimulation in biography
rubrics_metrics.description: Mr. Davis has produced in small compass an account of the life and work of Huxley that is at once readable and stimulating.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Biographies should be engaging and accessible, conveying character and significance without merely summarizing larger works.

rubrics_metrics.name: Skillful employment of source material / not a mere abstract
rubrics_metrics.description: It was inevitable that he should draw largely upon Mr. Leonard Huxley's biography... but the materials have been skilfully employed, and the book is far from being a mere abstract of the larger work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When relying on prior sources, synthesize and add value rather than merely condensing; demonstrate authorial selection and interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balanced portrayal of subject's qualities and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Huxley's energy, industry and fixity of purpose are brought into due prominence... It is probable that we here touch upon one of Huxley's limitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good critical biography highlights strengths and also candidly discusses limitations or blind spots.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid factual slips and textual errors
rubrics_metrics.description: There are certain slips in Mr. Davis's book which should be remedied in a future edition. We note a few, as follows: — Ephestia elutella (recte elutella) is not a 'small beetle,' but a Phycid moth... Huxley wrote 'inconceivable,' where Mr. Davis has 'concevable'; ... who is Scotus Erigenus?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure species identifications, quotations, names, and factual assertions are correct and carefully proofread; slips undermine authority and should be corrected in later editions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and intelligibility of laboratory instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: The apparatus required ... is described, and instructions for the carrying out of the measurements are given in an easily intelligible form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical lab manuals should describe apparatus clearly and give step-by-step, comprehensible instructions suitable for students and instructors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensiveness of experimental coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: The course is modelled on that of the Leipzig school... it may perhaps account for the omission of several important types of experimental exercises. In particular, electrochemical experiments involving the estimation and separation of the metals and the preparation of different classes of compounds afford many valuable applications of physicochemical principles, and the omission of chapters dealing with these phases of the subject is regrettable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Textbooks and practical guides should cover key experiment types relevant to the discipline; omission of important areas (e.g., electrochemistry) is a notable deficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Precise definition of technical terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Some difficulty may be experienced in interpreting what is meant by the term 'maximum apparent error' in the first chapter. With a vocabulary of errors in which relative, absolute, possible, probable, and apparent errors may be spoken of, a careful definition of terms is essential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define specialized or potentially ambiguous technical terms clearly to avoid reader confusion, especially in instructional texts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriateness of experimental materials and examples
rubrics_metrics.description: In the dilatometric determination of transition temperatures (p. 274), Glauber's salt is not nearly so suitable as some other substances for the purposes of a laboratory exercise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select experimental substances and materials that are suitable, safe, and pedagogically appropriate for lab exercises; avoid recommending suboptimal reagents or apparatus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of literature references when citing many investigations
rubrics_metrics.description: The entire omission of literature references to the large number of investigations by authors whose names are quoted is most unfortunate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When discussing prior work or many authors, include full references to allow verification and further reading; omission of citations is a serious shortcoming.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation fidelity and field-appropriate tone
rubrics_metrics.description: The translation is good, although it is not difficult to recognise in it the work of a medical man rather than that of a physical chemist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translations should preserve technical nuance and adopt the appropriate disciplinary voice; a translation that betrays a different professional perspective may mislead specialist readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on general principles over rote facts in teaching texts
rubrics_metrics.description: A distinctive feature of the lectures on inorganic chemistry is the authors' attempt to minimise the number of chemical compounds described, and to illustrate by carefully selected examples the most important general phenomena and the laws which regulate them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For students (e.g., medical students), emphasize understanding of general laws and relationships rather than exhaustive lists of isolated facts or compounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Price suitability for intended audience
rubrics_metrics.description: For 430 pages of elementary inorganic chemistry fifteen marks is a singularly high price to have to pay, and may be prohibitive to many would-be purchasers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider affordability relative to target readership; excessively high price may restrict accessibility and uptake.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial harmony in multi-author works
rubrics_metrics.description: This is the first instalment of a work which ... Each of the sections ... will be written by a different author. In the first volume there is undoubtedly a certain want of harmony in treatment of the subject-matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors should ensure coherence and consistent treatment across contributions in multi-author volumes to avoid jarring differences in style, scope, or depth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate depth and scope for the work's purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: In a treatise on practical mining, it is questionable whether it is possible to deal usefully with so comprehensive a subject or to give sufficient detail to render the geological manuals superfluous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Align the scope and depth of coverage with the stated purpose—don't promise encyclopedic treatment where practical, concise guidance is expected; avoid overreaching that dilutes usefulness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality and elegance of literary style
rubrics_metrics.description: The editor's literary style, too, is far from faultless. His opening sentence, for example, cannot be regarded as elegant in composition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good writing craft (clear, elegant sentences) improves readability and credibility; poor literary style can detract even from technically solid content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of accessible and practical terminology
rubrics_metrics.description: Mr. C. A. Seyler's new system of classification... does not seem likely to commend itself to practical men, who would probably find such expressions as 'sub-para-bituminous-pseudo-anthracitic species' somewhat cumbersome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid overly cumbersome, jargon-laden, or unnecessarily complex nomenclature that impedes practical use by target readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conciseness combined with practical richness
rubrics_metrics.description: The third section, on trial borings, which has been written by Mr. H. F. Bulman, is admirable. It contains as much practical information as could possibly have been compressed into thirty pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Valorize concise sections that nevertheless deliver dense, practical, usable information—brevity with substance is a virtue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of unpublished details and informative illustration metadata
rubrics_metrics.description: The value is increased by the introduction of hitherto unpublished details of cost, and by the fact that the illustrations, unlike others in the volume, have in every case an indication of the scale to which they are drawn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide novel or unpublished practical data where possible and ensure illustrations include essential metadata (e.g., scale) to make them maximally informative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mechanical production quality (proofreading, plate numbering, placement)
rubrics_metrics.description: In other respects, too, the mechanical execution of the work leaves room for improvement. Proper names are not always spelt correctly... the numbering of the plates was evidently altered after the text had been printed off, so that not a single reference in the text to the plates is correct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure careful proofreading, correct spelling of proper names, consistent and accurate plate numbering and logical placement of illustrations relative to text; production errors seriously reduce usability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Synthesis and engaging summary of a large subject area
rubrics_metrics.description: He has given a broad general view, sketching in with a few accurate and telling strokes the more prominent features of the landscape, so that the whole presents a satisfactory and attractive summary of the racial characteristics of an important section of the British Empire.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For broad-area surveys, aim to synthesize complex material into clear, vivid summaries that capture main features without excessive detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific methodological approach in ethnography
rubrics_metrics.description: Mr. Crooke adopts the only scientific method (too often neglected) of commencing at the bottom with the so-called aborigines and working upwards through the mixed tribes to the pure Indo-Aryan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt sound methodological ordering (e.g., start from foundational groups and proceed to derived/complex formations) to provide a scientifically robust account.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balanced treatment of controversial points and candour about limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: If we have criticised a few of Mr. Crooke's statements, we freely admit that they deal with points of detail, some of which are objects of controversy. We can strongly recommend his book to the general reader...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critics and authors should acknowledge controversies and limitations; balanced appraisal that notes minor disputes while endorsing overall merit is appropriate.
